header:
Date: 2027-01-18
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood Product), Markus Lee (Orion Eng Lead), Samantha Cho (Orion CTO), Nora Patel (Orion DevOps), Evan Brooks (Orion Security)
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request-logs debugging flows. Reviewed how traces and request logs map to production QPS profiles, how prefix/KV caching and batching affect latency/cost, and security/compliance controls for Private deployments (VPC/KMS/SSO). Agreed to share SOC2 and sample logs and to schedule a pilot kickoff next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we have about 50 minutes, we'll run through the console tracing and then do request logs and debugging flow. quick intro?
[00:08] Markus (Orion): hey thanks, i'm markus engineering lead, sam is our cto, nora handles infra, evan is security.
[00:12] Samantha (Orion CTO): hi all.
[00:14] Sofia (Redwood SE): great to meet you all, i'll do the demo and show how traces surface errors and how request logs tie back to token usage.
[00:20] Jordan (Redwood Product): i'll chime in on the optimization suggestions and cost insights.
[00:24] Alex: quick agenda, tracing -> error analysis -> request logs -> Q&A + next steps. ok sofia take it away.
[00:30] Sofia: all right screen share, um starting with the traces tab. this is a synthetic trace, you can see the request start time, model variant (we sometimes see name mangles in the transcript but it's gpt-3-like here), and per-step latency. so if you click an individual token event it shows kernel time, kv-cache hit rate, and queueing. you can filter by model, region, and route.
[01:05] Markus: can you point out kv-cache? we have a lot of long conversations and we want to ensure cache is used.
[01:10] Sofia: yeah the trace has a field 'kv_hit' and prefix cache flags, and we show a histogram of cache hits across recent requests. our runtime will do prefix/KV caching automatically when routes are configured. (murmur) sometimes the labels show 'KVcash' in older logs, transcription often mungs acronyms.
[01:30] Nora: how do we map this to our traffic though? we run 250 qps peak with a 95th token length around 450.
[01:36] Jordan: we can upload a traffic profile CSV or connect via our ingestion agent; once ingested the console can replay sampled traces and map to expected latency buckets. we'll also show batch sizing suggestions in Optimize.
[01:50] Evan (Security): on encryption, where are request logs stored and how do you handle PII? we need KMS, and retention controls.
[01:58] Alex: good question. for Private deployments request logs can live in the customer's VPC and integrate with customer KMS/HSM. for Hosted we encrypt at rest and support customer-managed keys on Dedicated seats; we'll send SOC2 and encryption doc.
[02:12] Samantha: also SSO and RBAC, we need SAML + SCIM provisioning.
[02:17] Alex: yes SAML/SSO + granular RBAC are supported, we'll include the SSO setup guide.
[02:22] Sofia: moving on, error analysis view shows grouped errors by signature and sample traces. e.g., you can see a tall tail of timeout errors and drill into request logs to see full prompt, token counts, and kernel stack. there is a quick link to re-run a request against another model variant for A/B.
[02:45] Markus: when you say 'timeout' is that app-level or infra-level? we saw '429' and 'internal error' spikes.
[02:51] Sofia: we tag errors into categories: client errors like malformed prompts, rate limit 429s, and runtime errors including OOM or kernel failure. trace will show either 'queue_wait' or 'runtime_error' with a stack snippet. sometimes the transcription will read 'O-O-M' as oom or 'Oh em' but the UI has the raw code.
[03:14] Nora: can we pull the exact request logs for a specific user id and timeframe? we need to recreate incidents.
[03:20] Sofia: yes you can query by trace id, route, user_id and we keep a per-route outgoing request id. request-logs export supports CSV/JSON and we've got pre-built Kibana/Datadog connectors. you can also stream logs to your S3 or GCS bucket.
[03:35] Evan: retention and audit logs? we need 1 year retention for logs for compliance.
[03:39] Alex: in Private you control retention; Hosted has tiered retention options as an add-on. audit logs for admin actions are stored and we can provide log exports for audits.
[03:48] Sofia: demoing a real trace now, expanding spans, you see time spent in tokenization, kernel execution, and output serialization. here's an example where batching increased throughput but introduced a 20ms median latency bump at tail.
[04:06] Jordan: right and Optimize will recommend lowering max_batch_size or changing batching window for low-latency routes. we show estimated cost delta as well.
[04:20] Markus: how accurate are the cost estimates? we run tight unit economics.
[04:24] Jordan: estimates are based on per-token runtime and region pricing plus measured batching efficiency; they're approximate but we've seen them be within 8-12% of production when traffic profile is provided.
[04:32] Sofia: i'm going to reproduce an incident; searching for trace id 7f3a... filter timeframe last 24h, found 12 related traces. opening a request log: you can see request headers, prompt, model hash, latency breakdown, and a base64 of the kernel error if present.
[04:49] Samantha: is that kernel error human-readable? our offline team needs stack to triage.
[04:52] Sofia: yes stack snippets are present; for privacy we mask PII by default, but you can toggle full payload for allowed roles or in Private deployments. masking rules are configurable.
[05:05] Nora: what about correlating traces to infra metrics, like GPU utilization?
[05:09] Jordan: we correlate with host metrics if you install the metrics exporter or connect cloud provider metrics. in Dedicated we can correlate per-pod GPU util to high-latency traces to highlight hot kernels.
[05:24] Alex: quick note, competitor comparisons: some customers move from raw endpoints like OpenAI to our Dedicated for better cost predictability; Anthropic and Cohere were mentioned in your RFP.
[05:33] Markus: yes we evaluated Anthropic for safety controls. how do you handle safety/regression monitoring?
[05:38] Sofia: we have quality monitoring tied to prompt sets/evals. the console can run periodic evals and alert on regressions post-deploy; you can attach a prompt set to a rollout to gate traffic.
[05:50] Markus: nice, that helps. back to request logs, can we slice by API key or route? we have internal services with different keys.
[05:56] Sofia: yes per-route, per-api-key, and per-customer filtering; RBAC controls who can view full payloads.
[06:05] Evan: what's the onboarding timeline for Private/VPC? we have strict network requirements and need air-gapped options.
[06:11] Alex: Private usually takes 6-8 weeks for an initial deployment with our infra team if on-prem air-gap is required; VPC deployments are faster (2-4 weeks) depending on network approvals.
[06:21] Samantha: is there an initial pilot we can do on Hosted or Dedicated to validate traces and traffic?
[06:25] Alex: yes we often do a 2-week pilot on Dedicated with a small reserved pool and real traffic sampling to validate latency and KV cache behavior.
[06:33] Markus: what about data egress and residency? our contracts require EU-only processing for some products.
[06:38] Alex: we can route requests to EU regions and keep logs in-region for Dedicated/Private; Hosted also offers region pinning for enterprise customers.
[06:46] Sofia: showing error grouping UI, you can pin a sample trace and create an issue that links to the trace and export payload for eng triage. here's the 'create incident' button that attaches the relevant logs.
[06:59] Nora: can we integrate with Jira/Slack?
[07:02] Sofia: yes we have webhooks and built-in integrations for Jira, Slack, and PagerDuty.
[07:08] Jordan: quick optimization example: for a chat route with 60% long prefix reuse, Optimize suggests enabling aggressive KV cache and switching to a quantized variant for cold starts; estimated cost reduction ~32% with sub-5% quality delta.
[07:26] Samantha: hmm what do you mean by 'quantized variant'? will accuracy degrade?
[07:31] Jordan: quantized variants use int8/int4 kernels; for many chat workloads quality impact is small but you'll want to run evals. Optimize can recommend which layers to quantize and give a predicted quality score.
[07:44] Markus: we need to validate that on our eval prompts.
[07:47] Jordan: we'll share the evaluation harness; you can run it against your prompt set and compare metrics.
[07:52] Sofia: going back to request logs export - here's the export dialog, you can schedule daily exports to S3 with KMS encryption and set retention lifecycle rules.
[08:05] Evan: does the export include the full prompt by default?
[08:08] Sofia: default is masked, you can choose full payload in Private or with appropriate roles. export format is newline-delimited JSON with trace_id, timestamp, route, api_key_hash, prompt_hash, token_counts, latency_breakdown, error_code.
[08:23] Alex: verbal recap of security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, VPC options, audit logs. we'll attach docs.
[08:29] Samantha: great.
[08:31] Sofia: last part, debugging workflow: when a customer reports an incident you search by trace_id or user_id, open grouped errors, reproduce request with re-run button, or reroute to a fallback model. you can also mark a deployment if a regression is found and rollback with canary controls.
[08:53] Markus: re-run, does that re-execute in prod model or in a sandbox?
[08:57] Sofia: you can choose -- re-run in a sandboxed replay environment or re-run in a controlled canary with limited traffic. replays are deterministic if you provide the exact seed and context.
[09:10] Nora: any concerns with GDPR when re-running?
[09:13] Alex: replays can be redacted and run in region; we advise keeping PII out of replays or ensuring proper legal coverage.
[09:20] [long demo silence as Sofia scrolls through multiple traces and exports, occasional murmur]
[15:02] Sofia: jumping ahead, here's a tail-latency analysis for the last 7 days — spikes correlate with a kernel update two weeks ago. you can annotate traces and correlate to deployment ids.
[15:20] Markus: so we can attribute a regression to a kernel or quantization change?
[15:24] Jordan: yes we tag traces with model build ids and kernel versions. that helps root-cause.
[15:30] Samantha: what's your SLA for Dedicated?
[15:33] Alex: Dedicated has a 99.9% uptime SLA and latency SLOs per route which we contractually commit in reserved capacity agreements.
[15:41] Evan: last question on access controls: can we set read-only for security folks and full-view for eng?
[15:45] Alex: yes RBAC supports role templates and custom roles, and SAML provisioning maps groups.
[15:50] Sofia: demo wrap-up. i'll share a sample request-log export and a trace bundle for your team to try.
[15:56] Markus: ok next steps?
[16:00] Alex: recap: we'll send SOC2 + SSO guide (Alex), sample logs and benchmark sheet (Sofia), and we'll schedule a pilot kickoff (Alex + Markus to agree on date).
[16:09] Samantha: sounds good. we'll aim to get traffic profile by 2027-01-21.
[16:13] Nora: i'll check with infra on S3 permissions and retention.
[16:17] Evan: and i'll review the security docs when you send them.
[16:21] Alex: thanks everyone. any final q's?
[16:24] Markus: none here, thanks.
[16:26] Alex: great, we'll follow up in email and book the kickoff. bye!
[16:30] [call ends, but recording continues as folks do post-call chatter and a short buffer period typical of call systems]
